text:
kevin: Quick sync — we're evaluating ipvlan vs NAT at the tenant edge for private endpoints. want to capture perf, operability, and upgrade path tradeoffs. thoughts?
morgan: IPvlan is interesting for source IP preservation and avoids SNAT hairpin. fewer tcp conn tracking issues. :+1:
sara: Danger: ipvlan ties you to host networking semantics and can be a headache with multi-AZ pod placement. can we preserve isolation guarantees?
ashley: Also need to consider ENI/secondary IP limits on AWS. ipvlan still needs host interfaces for tenant IPs — we hit limits if we allocate per-tenant IPs.
ben: NAT approach (SNAT/DNAT in a gateway) centralizes IP allocation and avoids ENI churn, but it loses client source IP unless we pass X-Forwarded-For at L7. Some customers care about true source IP for logging/ACLs.
kevin: right. summary so far: ipvlan = preserve source IP, lower perf overhead, more host-level coupling + IP quota. NAT = simpler host isolation, more state/tracking, more CPU for conntrack.
priya: have we measured conntrack CPU at scale? last spike during a customer test killed a node when we got 200k concurrent flows.
infra-bot: deploy-notification: ran perf-run v2 on staging at 2026-03-20 16:04:23 — results uploaded to /perf/runs/4923.
morgan: perf numbers from infra-bot: ipvlan path median p50 token-latency ~18ms, NAT path ~24ms, but NAT tail p99 spikes with many small conns.
sara: Operational shift: ipvlan means our relays must handle ARP and L2 considerations. Do we want to run a lightweight L2 agent on hosts? eBPF could help with isolation without full L2 bridging.
ben: eBPF + xdp for ingress policing might work, but we still need per-tenant routing rules. mixing eBPF + ipvlan could be complex to debug.
ashley: Upgrade/migration plan question: can we do NAT as default and flip high-needs tenants to ipvlan? That avoids immediate ENI explosion.
kevin: propose incremental plan: (1) build prototype ipvlan host agent (opt-in tenants) + test IP allocation model using private IP pools per-AZ, (2) add eBPF filters for isolation, (3) run chaos tests for AZ failover, (4) evaluate metrics (conntrack CPU, packet drop, latency).
priya: +1. add cost modeling: ENI/IP limits vs CPU cost for conntrack + potential extra obs for XFF handling.
morgan: small implementation note: use ipvlan L3 mode to avoid bridged L2 namespaces — keeps ARP simpler.
sara: question on TLS termination: with ipvlan we see client source IP at our relay, so we can preserve mTLS client cert mapping. with NAT we would have to propagate it at L7. which do we prefer for Private mode?
ben: for regulated customers I think preserving L3 source identity is a strong signal. we should document covenants for Private deployments: if you choose NAT, we require app-level headers for identity.
kevin: good call. I'll draft a short RFC that includes: design options, migration path, required host agent contract, metrics to collect, and a small experiment plan.
infra-bot: experiment-queue: created ticket INF-1387 for ipvlan prototype.
ashley: tiny ops note: make sure iptables conntrack limits bumped on prototype nodes or you'll see early OOMs.
priya: who wants to own the prototype?
kevin: I can lead the POC with morgan and ashley as co-owners. will post a short plan + milestones tomorrow.
morgan: I'll grab the perf harness and wire up conntrack/cpu budgets.
sara: ok, if you need a customer for beta we can try ACME Corp private cluster next week.
ben: let's also add a test to ensure egress billing attribution doesn't break when source IPs change.
kevin: noted. thanks everyone — will follow up with RFC link and a short checklist. :rocket:
